name: Performance Decrease Policy (AMD)
description: Chooses which signal is allowed to drop the clock back down, which changes how quickly the chip settles after a burst.

name: Performance Decrease Threshold (AMD)
description: How far utilisation must rise before the clock steps up.  A low value makes the boost policy respond sooner.

name: Performance Increase Policy (AMD)
description: Chooses which hardware performance boost signal is allowed to raise the clock, instead of letting the CPU decide.

name: Performance Increase Threshold (AMD)
description: How far utilisation must fall before the clock steps down.  A low value makes the boost policy respond sooner.

name: Minimum Unparked Cores (100%)
description: Asks the scheduler to keep every core out of the parked state, so spreading work does not stall on a waking core.

name: Processor Boost Mode
description: Sets the hardware turbo behaviour to aggressive, letting the chip exceed its sustained base clock for short bursts.

name: Energy Performance Preference
description: Biases the hardware scheduler toward performance over energy saving when it picks between equally valid cores.

name: Heterogeneous Scheduling (Performance)
description: Tells Windows to place long-running threads on the performance cores rather than letting it choose between P-cores and E-cores.

name: Short-Thread Scheduling (Performance)
description: Applies the same performance-core preference to short-running threads, which the long-thread policy deliberately leaves alone.

name: Disable Processor Idle States
description: Stops the processor dropping into its low-power C-states, keeping cores clocked up at the cost of idle power and heat.

name: Performance Decrease Policy (Intel)
description: Chooses which signal is allowed to drop the clock back down, which changes how quickly the chip settles after a burst.

name: Performance Decrease Threshold (Intel)
description: How far utilisation must rise before the clock steps up.  A low value makes the boost policy respond sooner.

name: Performance Increase Policy (Intel)
description: Chooses which hardware performance boost signal is allowed to raise the clock, instead of letting the CPU decide.

name: Performance Increase Threshold (Intel)
description: How far utilisation must fall before the clock steps down.  A low value makes the boost policy respond sooner.

name: Maximum Processor State
description: Lets the processor use its full advertised frequency instead of being held below the maximum by the power plan.

name: Minimum Processor State
description: Holds cores at full clock while the system is busy, trading idle power and heat for a floor under clock speed.

name: MMCSS Game Priority
description: Marks the game as a high-priority Multimedia Class Scheduler task so audio and video threads get dedicated CPU time.

name: Foreground Priority Boost
